articles.title: Recent Progress in Partially Coherent Structured Light
institutions: Fujian Institute of Research on the Structure of Matter
University of Chinese Academy of Sciences
articles.summary: Spatial coherence is evolving from a basic parameter describing the statistical properties of random optical fields into an important degree of freedom for structured-light manipulation. By engineering the degree of spatial coherence, correlation-amplitude distributions, and correlation-phase structures, a wide variety of partially coherent structured beams can be constructed, including vortex, Airy, Bessel, vector, and more complex statistical optical fields. In recent years, their generation has progressed from conventional random scattering to incoherent modal superposition, digitally programmable synthesis, and the active construction of complex spatial correlation structures. …

articles.title: Structured-light-mediated hybrid entanglement between photon polarization and electronic orbital angular momentum
Fourier pixels: unifying bidirectional vectorial light-field generation and sensing at the microscale
articles.authors: Haofan Huang, Zechen Wei, Puxiang Lai
articles.summary: This commentary highlights Fourier pixels, a recent advance in planar optics that enables continuous momentum space engineering and full vectorial light-field manipulation. By replacing discrete resonators with continuous surface topographies, Fourier pixels overcome the near-field coupling and phase discretization limits of classical metasurfaces, providing an alternative route to monolithic on-chip optical processing. They unify light generation and sensing in a single micrometer-scale pixel, enabling simultaneous, bidirectional control of amplitude, phase, and polarization. We discuss the principles, demonstrations, and challenges toward practical on-chip photonic technologies.

articles.title: High‐Performance Light‐Triggered Hydrogel Microvalve with Rigid Framework Structure for Microfluidics
articles.authors: Zeye Li, Hao Wu, Wei Tang, Wen Huang, Feng Tang, Chenchu Zhang, Yanlei Hu, Jiawen Li, Jiaru Chu, Dong Wu
institutions: School of Microelectronics Hefei University of Technology Hefei China
articles.summary: Light‐triggered hydrogel microvalves have attracted considerable interest in microfluidics owing to their remote actuation and biocompatibility. However, conventional microvalves based on homogeneous hydrogels are typically placed within microfluidic channels without a deep integrated bond and undergo uniform bulk contraction without structural constraints, leading to limited actuation amplitude and slow response, which restrict their practical applications in precise fluid manipulation. Here, we develop a framework‐structured light‐triggered hydrogel microvalve featuring a non‐deformable framework layer and a deformable valve layer with four petals. …

articles.summary: Magneto-optical traps (MOTs) provide a foundation for cold-atom technologies, but their optical delivery systems remain a major obstacle to miniaturization. This review evaluates metasurface-based MOT architectures through the requirements imposed by cooling-field geometry, polarization, and optical-power delivery. Pancharatnam-Berry-phase, propagation-phase, and hybrid-phase implementations are compared with grating and photonic-integrated-circuit-assisted systems using reported optical and atomic performance, with explicit distinctions between measured quantities, derived estimates, and unavailable data. …

articles.summary: Optical skyrmions and bimerons are topologically protected vector textures that can be constructed from diverse optical vector fields. As robust information carriers in free space, these topological textures have seen their generation methods evolve from complex optical systems toward integrated meta-devices. Despite significant advancements in generating skyrmions and bimerons across various optical frequency bands, a single monolithic integrated device for the generation and dynamic switching of diverse topological quasiparticles in the terahertz (THz) regime remains elusive. …

articles.summary: Perfect vector vortex beams (PVVBs) have emerged as a powerful platform for high-dimensional information processing, high-capacity optical communications and encryption. To further expand the information capacity of PVVBs, collaborative manipulation of their multiple degrees of freedom under multi-wavelength multiplexing is an effective strategy. However, previous studies on the generation of PVVBs are typically limited to a single wavelength, rendering it difficult to simultaneously control more than two degrees of freedom across different wavelength channels. …

articles.summary: Tilted fiber Bragg gratings (TFBGs) are important in‐fiber components for sensing, polarization control, and ultrafast photonics, yet their scalable fabrication remains limited by the trade‐off between writing speed, angular flexibility, and spectral quality. Here we report an SLM‐enabled femtosecond line‐focus inscription strategy for ultrafast, angle‐programmable fabrication of TFBGs. …

articles.summary: Time‐varying photonic structures redistribute electromagnetic energy among Floquet harmonics, enabling frequency conversion, nonreciprocity, parametric gain, and dynamic wavefront control. Accurate modeling of realistic platforms remains challenging when temporal modulation occurs in strongly dispersive materials, because each harmonic experiences a distinct material response while remaining coupled to all others through the modulation. This work introduces a full‐wave harmonic‐balance framework for dispersive time‐varying photonic structures. …

articles.summary: Optical neural networks (ONNs), particularly diffractive neural networks (DNNs), offer a promising computational paradigm owing to their high speed, intrinsic parallelism, and low energy consumption. However, most demonstrated DNNs are static, with their functionalities fixed after fabrication. Although several reconfigurable architectures such as spatial light modulators (SLMs) and electrically controlled digital‐coding metasurfaces have been demonstrated, they often suffer from high power consumption and limited scalability. …
